feature: Zoom callouts make room for each other
summary: A new zoom callout now lands clear of the callouts already on the picture instead of dropping on top of the last one. Draw three details in a row and you get three readable boxes, not a pile you have to untangle by hand.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. Nothing to turn on. Open any screenshot.

try.do: Press the Zoom Callout tool in the tool bar.
Drag a box around a detail near the left of the picture.
Press the Zoom Callout tool again and drag a box around the detail just below the first one.
Check that the second magnified box landed somewhere clear rather than on the first.
Repeat once more, a third detail below the second.
Drag one of the callouts away by hand, then draw a fourth: the new one steers around where you just put it.

evaluate: When the second box appears, can you read both callouts without moving anything?
Does the box fly to a spot you would have chosen yourself, or does it feel like it ran away from the detail it is magnifying?
On the third and fourth callout, is the picture still legible, or is it time for callouts to line up in a column instead of hunting free space?
Is the flight from the source box to the placed box still easy to follow now that it sometimes travels further?
rough: On a crowded picture a callout can end up a fair distance from the detail it magnifies: staying readable beats staying close, and the leader lines are what carry the connection. Worth judging whether that trade reads right at four or more callouts.

Only the magnified boxes count as occupied. The thin outline drawn around a source detail does not, so a new box can cover an earlier callout's source ring. Treating those as obstacles too would send new callouts much further away for a small gain, so it was left out on purpose.

When the picture is genuinely full, the box keeps the spot it would have taken before rather than hunting the least-buried one. That keeps a crowded canvas predictable, but it does mean the very last callout on a busy picture can still land on another one.
